classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicitly sequenced parts to derive literal tangent and cosine formulas, substitute into triangle area, equate the two areas and apply inverse tangent; the earlier parts supply the relationships needed later.

content.prompt: The cross-section through the centre of a diamond cut at The Perfect Diamond Company is of the shape shown in the diagram. Region $A$ is semicircular and region $B$ is an isosceles triangle. The semicircle has radius $r$ mm and the isosceles triangle has height $h$ mm, slant height $s$ mm and slant angle $\theta$, as shown.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle above a semicircle sharing its diameter. The altitude joins apex to midpoint. Matching double ticks identify equal sloping sides; dimension arrows label the sloping side, altitude and radius. Ordinary source blue outlines and the red midpoint marker are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The triangle has base 2r, perpendicular height h and equal sloping sides s. Its left base angle is theta. Region A is the semicircle and region B is the triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and geometry are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

answer.worked:
Equating the areas gives
$$\begin{align*}r^2\tan\theta&=\frac12\pi r^2\\\tan\theta&=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{align*}$$
The radius is positive, so division by $r^2$ is valid.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Solve the equation in part c to find the value of $\theta$ for diamonds cut at The Perfect Diamond Company. Round off your answer to the nearest tenth of a degree.

answer.worked:
Using inverse tangent in degree mode:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\\\theta&\approx57.5184^\circ\\\theta&\approx57.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find, to two decimal places, the total area of the cross-section through the centre of a diamond if the radius, $r$, is 2 mm.

answer.worked:
The two regions have equal areas, so the total is twice the semicircle’s area.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{total}}&=2\left(\frac12\pi r^2\right)\\A_{\text{total}}&=\pi(2)^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=4\pi\text{ mm}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&\approx12.57\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
